metadata.case_name: CHUNG LAI HA v. CHING MEI YEE

plaintiff.occupation_before: Superintendent of Posts, manager of the Sheung Wan Post Office
plaintiff.occupation_after: Retired (early retirement December 2010; left employment 7 May 2011)

injuries.description: multiple contusions and abrasion, bruise and soft tissue injury on her face, neck and chest wall
source: Physical examination of the plaintiff after the Incident showed multiple contusions and abrasion, bruise and soft tissue injury on her face, neck and chest wall.
As a result of the Incident, the plaintiff developed psychiatric symptoms of PTSD with moderate intensity.

manifestations.description: abrasion and scratch mark in the face, small abrasion in upper lip, bruises in both arms and in chest
tense / anxiety / symptoms of hyperarousal or marked anxiety
recurrent flashback of the Incident / re-experiencing the traumatic event
avoidance of the assault venue / avoiding reminders of the trauma
unable to continue with her work at the Hongkong Post; early retirement

treatments_received: A&E treatment at Queen Mary Hospital (diagnosed with multiple contusions)
Consultation with Dr Danny PK Ma (9 July 2009)
Examination and follow-up at Tseung Kwan O Hospital (10 July 2009 and follow-ups)
Psychiatric treatment and medications at United Christian Hospital (from 13 July 2009 and follow-ups)
Psychiatric treatment, counseling and antidepressant prescribed by Dr Peter WT Yu (first seen 30 September 2009; antidepressant until November 2010)
treatments_future: Continuous psychiatric treatment and counseling for at least three more years
Counseling at 12-week intervals as suggested by Dr Yu

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Before the Incident, she played squash and enjoyed travelling. After the Incident, because of the psychiatric symptoms suffered by her, she lost interest in travelling and participating in other activities which she used to enjoy.
She avoided interacting with friends and people in her social circle after the Incident.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: She developed intense fear that the Incident would happen again, felt unsafe at home and at workplace, and avoided the assault venue; she sold her Tseung Kwan O property and moved district because she felt unsafe.
Because of psychiatric illness she was unable to continue with her work at the Hongkong Post and opted for early retirement.
